messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — customer 'Orchid' private deploy failed our isolation smoke tests after the RBAC tweak yesterday. KMS requests from the model-serving pool are getting 403s but jumpbox can reach KMS just fine. Any ideas?
Maria L.: which RBAC change specifically? the one that added `serviceAccount: inference-pool` to cross-tenant-access?
Alex Chen: yes, that change. We expected the KMS policy binding `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the tenant key to cover it. logs show 'permission denied' at the RPC layer.
Samir: can you paste the exact audit log entry? might be an IAM mismatch (principal vs service account email).
Alex Chen: pasted below from stackdriver (redacted):
```
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "serviceAccount:inference-pool@orchid-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
protoPayload.methodName: "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
protoPayload.status: { code: 7, message: "Permission denied" }
resource.labels.key_ring: "projects/orchid-prod/locations/us-central1/keyRings/ri-kr"
```
Maria L.: hm — the binding uses `serviceAccount:inference-pool@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (our org SA) not the tenant-scoped SA. cross-tenant SA needs explicit grant.
Jordan: that's on purpose — we wanted tenant isolation. If we grant tenant SA direct KMS access we weaken isolation guarantees. Can we instead route KMS ops through a proxy in our control plane?
Samir: proxy would preserve isolation but adds blast radius if compromised. Alternative: add a short-lived credential exchange where our control plane mints a signed JWT for the tenant runtime to call KMS via our gateway. That keeps keys owned by tenant, ops go through our auditable path.
Alex Chen: architecture-wise sounds good. Two followups: 1) audit logging — we need per-tenant, per-request KMS audit entries in customer logs (not only central logs). 2) network policy — confirm we have egress locked so tenant nodes can't talk to KMS directly unless via gateway.
Maria L.: for audit: enable KMS DATA_ACCESS logs at tenant project level + export to tenant's secure logging sink. Need to add a filter to include protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail so we can map service account to runtime.
Jordan: for netpol: current Calico policy allows egress to 10.0.0.0/8 and a small set of cloud APIs. We need a deny-all and explicit allow to our gateway IPs and KMS endpoint. I'll add a draft.
Samir: also run a vuln triage on the proxy code path — especially token exchange and replay protection. Add HMAC/nonce, short ttl tokens, and strict audience checks.
Alex Chen: putting action items: (a) Maria to add KMS DATA_ACCESS log export config for tenant projects, (b) Jordan to propose netpol YAML that restricts egress to gateway+kms, (c) Samir to design the short-lived credential flow and threat model, (d) Ops to run a simulated breach to ensure tenant nodes cannot call KMS directly.
Maria L.: on it — I'll open the infra-change PR and link to the log sink config.
Jordan: draft netpol snippet: 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress-to-kms-gw
spec:
  podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: "inference-runtime" } }
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock: { cidr: "203.0.113.10/32" }  # gateway
    - ipBlock: { cidr: "198.51.100.5/32" } # cloud-kms endpoint
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Jordan: will iterate, but need ops-bot to approve scheduled rollout window.
ops-bot: Noted. Can we do canary 10% on staging then 100% in low-traffic window? Need at least 2-hour maintenance window.
Samir: for the credential exchange: idea is 1) tenant runtime calls our auth endpoint with mutual TLS, 2) auth endpoint validates and returns a signed ephemeral token (audience: kms-gateway, ttl: 5m), 3) runtime calls kms-gateway with token, gateway mints real KMS call with service identity. We'll add nonce and single-use constraints.
Alex Chen: sounds good. Also add regression tests that simulate RBAC misconfig (missing grant) to ensure the gateway path still works and logs are generated.
Maria L.: I'll attach checklist in the PR: netpol, log sinks, gateway auth, tests, canary plan.
Jordan: quick question — does this model affect latency SLA? a 5-10ms extra hop acceptable?
Samir: should be within SLA if gateway is colocated; we can bench. I'll run load tests.
Alex Chen: thanks all. If anything blocks, ping me. Filing a short incident doc in #incidents with summary and mitigation steps.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-047. Severity: P2. Assigned: Alex Chen, Maria L., Samir.
Alex Chen: closing the loop — scheduling tabletop next Tue to walk through the simulated breach and KMS token flow.
